messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
We're moving the platform to a new infrastructure provider starting next quarter.

The current setup has hit limits on capacity and response time during peak load. The new platform fixes both, with the same features and interface you use now.

Migration happens in stages. We move accounts in batches over several weeks, starting with a small group in early Q4 and expanding from there. You'll get a notice with your specific migration date at least two weeks in advance.

During your migration window, expect a maintenance period of under an hour. We schedule these outside business hours in your account's time zone. Data, settings, and integrations carry over automatically — no action needed on your end.

API endpoints stay the same. If you use webhooks or direct API integrations, no code changes are required. Rate limits increase by 3x on the new platform.

For accounts on legacy authentication methods (API keys issued before 2024), you must switch to OAuth 2.0 before your migration date. We'll flag affected accounts in the notice email.

After migration, you'll see the new platform status page and updated dashboard metrics. Historical data and reports remain accessible in full.

Support during the transition: our team monitors each migration batch in real time and rolls back any account that hits an issue within the first 24 hours.

Questions about your specific migration date or account status go to support@[company].com, subject line "Platform Migration."

We'll follow up with exact dates for your batch as Q4 approaches.
